title: SLA-tiered lease-extension and soft-yield policy for continuous batching
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: During sustained hotset traffic we see repeated hard preemptions that evict KV entries and fragment GPU memory, causing latency spikes for P0 and high-SLA tenants. Goals: reduce tail latency for SLA-tiered tenants, lower KV churn for hot keys, and avoid gross GPU memory fragmentation while preserving fairness across tenants. Proposal: implement a SLA-tiered lease-extension mechanism combined with a soft-yield preemption policy. Each request receives a short-lived KV lease token when it is admitted to a batch; high-SLA tenants (SLA tiers Gold/Platinum) can automatically request short lease extensions on imminent eviction events (grace window 50-200ms). Instead of immediate hard eviction, the preemptor will attempt soft-yielding: it notifies lower-priority in-flight batches to yield capacity (e.g., stop owning new KV allocations and finish current micro-batches), and performs transient KV compaction to reclaim small contiguous memory ranges before evicting entries. This reduces jitter from repeated load-migrate-evict cycles. The policy includes a decay-based credit system so tenants that frequently request extensions pay a longer backoff before re-grant, preventing starvation of best-effort workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Gold/SLA tenants see 40-60% reduction in P99 tail latency under sustained 95th-percentile hotset load compared to baseline preemption
KV churn (evictions/sec) on hot partitions drops by at least 30% in our GPU memory simulation with lease-extension enabled
No regression in average throughput for best-effort tenants > -10% under mixed workloads
Automated canary rollout completes with rollback threshold defined (P99 increase > 15% for Gold tenants triggers rollback)
End-to-end integration tests and load sims merged to CI and run on pull requests
implementation_notes: Introduce LeaseToken struct in batch admission path (small fixed-size header attached to request metadata)
Extend eviction notifier to publish imminent-eviction events to tenant controllers with 50-200ms configurable grace window
Add soft-yield hook into continuous batcher to allow ongoing micro-batches to finish and avoid taking new KV reservations for X ms
Implement transient KV compactor that coalesces small free regions in GPU memory before choosing eviction candidates
Credit decay: per-tenant counter increments on each granted extension; decay half-life configurable (default 60s) to avoid long-term starvation
Expose config flags behind runtime-1.19 feature gate for canary rollout
test_plan: Unit tests for LeaseToken lifecycle and credit accounting
Microbench harness: synthetic hotset with Zipfian key distribution, measure evictions/sec and P99 latency across SLA tiers
Integration test in nightly cluster with mixed tenants (Gold, Standard, BestEffort) to validate fairness guarantees
Chaos test: force repeated KV allocation spikes and verify soft-yield reduces full eviction cycles
Performance regression tests to ensure throughput impact is within target (-10% max for best-effort)
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind runtime-1.19; start with canary on dedicated capacity pool (internal dev tenants)
Stage 1: 5% of traffic for Gold tenants + internal nightlies for 48h
Stage 2: 25% traffic for mixed tenant profiles for 72h, monitor eviction and latency metrics
Stage 3: 100% rollout for Gold + opt-in for Standard, keep BestEffort default off until further tuning
Rollback criteria: P99 for Gold increases > 15% or evictions/sec increase > 20% vs baseline
monitoring_and_metrics: Per-tenant P50/P95/P99 latency by SLA tier
Lease_extension_grants and Lease_extension_denials, with per-tenant credit counts
Throughput (tokens/sec) per tenant class and overall cluster throughput
